approved: Veterans’ Affairs Legislation Amendment (Mental Health and Other Measures) Bill 2014
Written by a model from the explanatory memorandum; not the record
The bill would change the Veterans' Entitlements Act from 1 July 2014 to broaden who can get free mental health care and which conditions qualify.

It would extend non-liability health care to cover alcohol and substance use disorders, and to include former Australian Defence Force members who served for at least three years and were discharged because they could not perform their duties.
The expansion applies to those with three or more years of continuous full-time peacetime service starting on or after 7 April 1994, including those with service both before and after that date.
Adds alcohol use disorder and substance use disorder to the list of conditions covered by non-liability health care.
Extends eligibility for non-liability mental health care to certain former Australian Defence Force members.
Sets the qualifying service period at three years of continuous full-time peacetime service starting on or after 7 April 1994.
Veterans and former Australian Defence Force members with qualifying service.

Cited Department of Veterans' Affairs figures showing 1,713 recent veterans suffer PTSD, praised the Soldier On support organisation founded in 2012 after the death of Lieutenant Michael Fussell, and warned that changing pension indexation to CPI only would have left a single veteran pension $60 a fortnight, or $1,560 a year, worse off over the past four years.

Detailed that 72,376 Australians have been deployed on operations since 1999, said non-liability mental health care will from 1 July 2014 extend to peacetime veterans by removing the current 7 April 1994 cutoff date, and outlined new alternative dispute resolution powers for the Veterans' Review Board.

Argued in support of the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Mental Health and Other Measures) Bill 2014, citing a University of Adelaide finding that 22 per cent of the ADF population, 11,016 people, had experienced a mental health disorder in the past year, and welcomed the bill's removal of the 7 April 1994 peacetime service cut-off for non-liability healthcare eligibility.

Argued in support of the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Mental Health and Other Measures) Bill 2014, noting the non-liability healthcare expansion costs $14.6 million over four years and the counselling service eligibility expansion costs $6.4 million over four years, and described the anxiety her family felt while her brother served two tours in Afghanistan.

Argued in support of the bill's mental health measures, citing Department of Veterans' Affairs data that as at March 2013 about 148,700 veterans held an accepted service-related disability, of whom about 46,400 had an accepted mental health disability, most commonly anxiety, depression or alcohol dependence.

Argued in support of the Veterans' Affairs Legislation Amendment (Mental Health and Other Measures) Bill 2014, recounted the 1945 Kapooka training explosion that killed 26 personnel, and noted that from 1 July 2015 Defence Force Retirement Benefits Scheme superannuants aged 55 and over will have pensions indexed like age and service pensions.

Argued in support of the bill's mental health measures, stated that post-traumatic stress disorder affects about one million Australians a year and 12 per cent will experience it in their lifetime, and said the ADF has lost more than 60 members to suicide since 2003, about half the toll from Afghanistan front-line deaths over the same period.

Argued in support of the bill, said this year more than $166 million will be spent on dedicated mental health services for veterans and their families, and disclosed his own long-term use of antidepressants while describing the stigma facing Defence personnel who report mental health issues.

Argued in support of the bill, citing the government's $12.3 billion commitment to veterans, and said Defence Force Retirement Benefits Scheme and Defence Force Retirement and Death Benefits Scheme pensions will be indexed by CPI, PBLCI and MTAWE from 1 July 2014 for superannuants aged 55 and over.
